utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Madam Registrar. If you could call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. All the accused are here. From the Defence teams I only notice the absence of Mr. Ostojic. What's become of Mr. Ostojic, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's become of Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Ostojic is in Chicago, and he should be back Monday. He had some personal affairs to attend to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. The Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Nicholls. The witness is already in his place. Good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we are going to proceed with your testimony. You're still testifying of course pursuant to the solemn declaration that you made yesterday. Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, in the Blagojevic case, when you testified in 2004, this was on page 9845, when you talked about the transport of men on the 12th of July 1995, which took place on the 12th of July 1995, you said that you did not know how many people exactly had boarded the buses but there were over 50 people per bus; is that right? Do you remember that that is what you said in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That more than 50 were boarded.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yesterday, on page 22 of the transcript, you said that there were 70 people and not 50. I understand that 70 is over 50, but this is quite an exact figure. Why didn't you mention the fact that there were 70 people in the Blagojevic case?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't asked to go into detail. In that testimony it was said over 50. Well 51 is over 50 too but I tried to be helpful here and explain how it was since I was there, and I'm sure that this is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: All right. Nonetheless, in the Blagojevic case, you did say or you mentioned that there were 50 people, and more than 50, and you are saying today that the figure is higher. How come that three years after your testimony, you are able to be more accurate than you were then?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are right. And even yesterday, he said that it was between 50 and 70. He couldn't be quite sure. So I think we have covered that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I agree that the witness did say this yesterday, but in the Blagojevic case, the witness never mentioned the figure of 70, so my question runs as follows: How come that this figure has now come to the forefront. But I shall not belabour the point and I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Fauveau. Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, witness.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Miodrag Stojanovic and together with my colleagues I defend Ljubomir Borovcanin. I should like to go through several documents in order to clarify some matters. If my understanding is correct, based on what you said yesterday, the whole day on the 12th and the 13th of July, you were in Potocari recording the numbers of the population being evacuated; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You went to perform this assignment because Momir Nikolic told you to report to Colonel Jankovic who in turn issued you with this specific order; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From that point on, when you reported to Colonel Jankovic, and you spoke of this in the Blagojevic case at page 9766 and 9767, you understood yourself to be subordinated to Colonel Jankovic in carrying out this specific assignment that was given to you?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In those two days, namely the 12th and the 13th, in Potocari, did you see Colonel Jankovic together with Major or Captain Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me more closely what your personal understanding was? What sort of duties did Colonel Jankovic carry out in Potocari on the 12th and the 13th? What was your impression as to his tasks?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained this in great detail. I don't know if there is any need for me to repeat what I said. I told you what he did, what I saw him do. I didn't give you my impressions. I told you what he did, in what way, and for how long and I still stand by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Janjic and Mr. Stojanovic, please allow a short pause between question and answer because there was some overlapping already, and I would like to avoid it as much as we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us try and be mindful of that, both of us, because we speak the same language. I would like us to look at Defence Exhibit 4D00016. We already had an opportunity to look at the document. This is the plea agreement and statement of facts of Momir Nikolic. We need to look at item 5 of his statement which is at page 2 of both the English and B/C/S versions. Let us focus on that part of his statement. Before this appears on our screens, I want to take you back to what you told us about the position of Colonel Jankovic. Let us clarify any remaining dilemmas that there may be. Can we please have item 5 on the screen? Thank you. Sir, please look at the first paragraph where Momir Nikolic states the following when speaking of the 12th of July and of the meeting at Fontana. That was the third meeting. And he says the following: "After the third meeting," do you see that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Item 5, paragraph 1 --

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the first paragraph doesn't start with that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's the second sentence. Do you see that now?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: "After the third meeting Colonel Jankovic came out of the Hotel Fontana and told me to coordinate the transportation of all women and children and the separation of able-bodied Muslim men." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, in view of what you personally know, and in view of what you've just read, that at that time, Jankovic was both by rank and by virtue of his position there, superior to Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to comment upon that. I didn't hear of this, of this encounter of theirs and these comments made. I don't want to comment or speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You say you don't want to speculate or comment upon that. I would take this as your position in terms of you not knowing anything about it and that's why you don't want to comment upon that?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever I would have to say about that would be speculation. I have no knowledge of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would I be right in saying that Colonel Jankovic issued you with that particular assignment because he wanted to arrive at the number of the evacuated population through counting the people leaving Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He issued me with a specific assignment, which I accepted, which I did. Now, as to what his initial or final goal may have been, I don't know. I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we have a look at the same document but the following page, and the following paragraph of item 6 of the plea agreement by Momir Nikolic? And that's page 3. Let us look at the last sentence of the first paragraph where Momir Nikolic states the following: He lists the units that were in Potocari on that day, and he goes on to say that in coordination, in coordinated action with these units, he coordinated and monitored the transportation of women and children to Kladanj and the separation and detention of able-bodied Muslim men. Do you see this portion of his statement?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony in the Blagojevic case, at page 9781, lines 10 to 21, you said that on the 12th of July you saw Momir Nikolic in Potocari. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is there a single reason why you should not believe Momir Nikolic and his statement which concerns himself?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a thousand reasons why I should not believe Momir Nikolic. I really cannot comment upon this. I don't see how I could comment upon that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm quite content with your answer, and I don't want to you comment upon matters you are unable to comment upon. If you look at the preceding line, it says there that this coordinated action and monitoring was carried out by Momir Nikolic in relation to the units that he listed there, and among them there is the military police of the Bratunac Brigade as well. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Military police of the Bratunac Brigade. And the civilian police with the Alsatians. Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of your knowledge and on the basis of what you saw, did the military police of the Bratunac Brigade take part in the activities during those two days in separating the able-bodied Muslim men in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present throughout the two days, and I can state with responsibility that the military police did not participate in any way in separating the able-bodied Muslim men from women, as you put it. Now, it is true that the military police was present there for those two days and that they had indeed their assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If you had assignments, as you put it a moment ago, can you tell us what were these specific assignments that they had based on what you saw and what you know?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the specific assignments are concerned, I will start by myself and will then refer to my colleagues. I told you what I did those two days. I'm a military police man and that was my duty. That's how I see it. I explained extensively that for the first hour, hour and a half or two, the time isn't that important, the counting, meaning the job that I did, was also done by other colleagues. After that, I explained that from that same locality, my colleagues, policemen, sat in a car and went to somewhere that I didn't know where they were going at the time. That was an assignment in my view. I also mentioned that the following day, the 13th, they were escorting buses to Bratunac. And I believe that I've mentioned sufficient assignments. These are the assignments I knew of and I observed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I told you that thanks to the Prosecution we are in possession of statements by several members of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade, I will mention only some, Rankic Petko, Bucalina Desimir, Francic Zlatko, who claimed that on the 12th of July, they had received an order from Momir Nikolic to do the following: From the Zuti Most, the Yellow Bridge where I quote, they were providing security to the bridge, to go to Potocari and assist their colleagues from the military police and members of the DutchBat, in order to make sure that the Muslim population could board buses without delay, would these statements refresh your memory as to their participation in the assignments and the carrying out of these obligations given by Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you this: I would not wish to comment upon the statements of the policemen that you refer to. You're repeating merely what I said, and that's that the military police helped escort the buses to Bratunac. I said that a couple of seconds ago. That's at least how I understood what you said, that at some point, a larger number of the military police, not only myself, were engaged in counting the population boarding the buses. I don't recall seeing the individuals you referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We heard that, but the question was not to comment upon his statement. My question was whether you would find this a confirmation of what you remember or whether this would refresh your memory, whether you saw that members of the military police boarded the Muslim population without delay on to buses, thus assisting members of the DutchBat in doing the same thing, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, the individuals you refer to were not members of the military police, in terms of paper work, yes, but they were never part of the military police I was a member of, and believe me when I tell you that they weren't there on that day. Their position was at Zuti Most. They may have gone there out of curiosity but I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you want to tell us -- first of all tell us by name, do you know the three individuals?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zlatko Francic, professor or teacher, Jovic [phoen] should also be among them. The individuals who were listed as members of the military police, but they never entered the military police building. I never saw them there. They're quite clearly -- they were stationed at Zuti Most where UNPROFOR soldiers passed. I don't know much about that but they worked at the -- at Zuti Most at the UNPROFOR check-point there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was Momir Nikolic in a position to issue orders to these persons to go to Potocari and assist to DutchBat in facilitating the departure of Muslim population without delay and boarding them on to buses? Could Momir Nikolic issue such an order to them?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that order. But I know that I never saw it, and I can't help you in answering whether he was in a position to issue such an order. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know a soldier from the platoon of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade by the name of Nenad Djokic?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him and I believe that I have mentioned him in my statements. Yes, I did mention his name and I know him very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th and 13th of July, did you see him at Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent a night with him, one of the nights, at the Fontana Hotel. I remember him well. But I cannot say whether I saw him at Potocari. I cannot remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I repeat to you that in this very courtroom, we heard the testimony of a protected witness and it was on November 6, 2006, on page 3608, and the brother of that person was singled out at Potocari, and this separation was performed by Nenad Djokic. My question would be whether such a testimony would refresh your memory whether or not it was possible that Nenad Djokic, as member of the military police of Bratunac Brigade, participated in the separation of able-bodied Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for Nenad Djokic, I gave you my answer. I was with him during the entire evening in front of the Fontana, in the night of the 12th to the 13th, and this is all I can tell you about Nenad Djokic. Whether or not he was in the position to do this or that, I cannot speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me, then, that you simply cannot rule out the possibility that that witness told the truth, because you didn't see him?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise but if I may, I would not venture into commenting the statement of that witness. I cannot rule it out, but I cannot say anything else about it either. I cannot comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You have mentioned the name of Milan Gvozdenovic, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we just get a spelling of that so we can clear it up? It's a difficult one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll try to go slower, Gvozdenovic, G-V-O-Z-D-E-N-O-V-I-C, Milan. Thank you. I'll repeat once more for the transcript. Gvozdenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that Milan Gvozdenovic was a member of the platoon of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade and that on July 12th and 13th, he was in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of the military police platoon, yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There was a second part to the question, whether he was in Potocari, whether you saw him in Potocari. Mr. Janjic, did you see him in Potocari on the 12th and 13th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may not -- not have given a complete answer. I understood the question to be whether he was there all day on the 12th and the 13th. And yes, I know him, he was there on the 12th and the 13th, but I cannot say whether he was there all day on those dates stated but he was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that at the times you saw him, he also was in -- he also participated in the recording of the persons leaving Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether he was performing that task, whether he assisted me in the first hour and a half, whether he was part of that group, because I said that they didn't all do that, but I'm sure that he was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he, at any moment, work on the registering of the number of people leaving Potocari, as you did?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was present but I don't remember. But we are talking only about an hour and a half or two hours on the 12th. At the time, some other members of the police were engaged in that activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who was entitled, in the system, to issue him an order to carry out certain assignments in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot testify about the system of command, because yesterday it was mentioned that it may not be normal, that the chain of command, when we were mentioning Momir Nikolic, to my understanding the commander of the platoon could have done that, Momir Nikolic or the deputy could have given an order to us, police, military policemen, and I wouldn't like to go further.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I have in front of me the transcript of your statement given on February the 5th, 2007, to the Public Prosecution Office of Bosnia-Herzegovina. On page 18 of the B/C/S version, you see said, "I forgot to say that all the time, with me, Gvozdenovic, Milan participated in the counting, and he submitted a list of that counting. He was there. I remember now." Does this part of your statement given on the 5th of February remind you whether or not this member of the Bratunac Brigade was -- engaged in certain activities in Potocari, namely the counting of people?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood your question. I mentioned the counting but I -- I was counting. I didn't mean to say that he was counting. While I was there counting, I remember that Milan Gvozdenovic was there, and then I go on to elaborate that I contacted him and that I -- that we had some common tasks, but what you are saying must have been said subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that by a decision of this Court, which is in force, Colonel Blagojevic was pronounced guilty because members of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade participated in the separation of persons? Have you read that, that decision?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't. I don't -- I'm not even familiar with the Prosecution -- with the indictment, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you about this any further. Did you on that day, July the 12th, in Potocari, see other members of the Bratunac Brigade, to be more concrete, the 2nd and 3rd Battalion of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have given detailed statements about that. Briefly, in passing by, I think you have it all in detail. I don't want to take away your precious time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Then your answer would be "Yes, I saw them on July 12th, the way I have described in more detail earlier"?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you add that comment, as I described in more detail earlier, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now take a look at Exhibit number P00220. It's a document that we were able to see yesterday. The log of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade, dated July 12 and 13th, the B/C/S version page 16, ERN number 00663925, page 13 [Realtime transcript read in error "16"] of the English version. And while we are waiting for this to be put on the screen, I'll remind you that this is the document that you saw yesterday when you were questioned by the Defence of Mr. Nikolic. In the English version it's page 13 because it seems that the transcript reads page 16. So it's actually page 13. Can you see it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke about this yesterday and if I remember well, you said that some information here is not correct, such as, that you personally, on those days, July the 12th and 13th, were not on the bridge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that you think that this log was written subsequently, after the events. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated my opinion. I said that this may be dated wrongly, but this is only my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So you think that this was actually written subsequently, after the event?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the content of this entry is not correct and I said why I think so. And I stand by that opinion that I uttered.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And then to continue, do you still think that this was done after the event as you said yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said so even today. Either the date is wrong or the information transmitted is wrong. I can't explain it. But there is -- there are errors in the text. I cannot say more because I have no knowledge about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What I want to ask you is: To your knowledge, can you explain in any way if this reads: "The police was engaged in the securing of UNHCR," what can this be about?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered yesterday, I can repeat if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Mr. Stojanovic, yesterday he made it very clear that he ruled out in an absolute manner any intervention or any protection directed towards UNHCR. So there is no point in asking him because that has already been ruled out already.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you allow, I have this part of the witness's statement that he gave yesterday in front of me, but I would like to hear whether this is his opinion or whether this is his precise knowledge because he knew where exactly each military police member was at any given moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So, is this your opinion, sir, or do you know that this didn't happen that way?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you read my statement, it will be all clear to you. So I must repeat what I said: I have no knowledge about the UNHCR. And for me to speculate about that organisation would be speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will never ask to you speculate, only to say something with which you can help us. And the following: The police worked on the handing over of the Muslim population to the Serbian fighters at Bratunac. You spoke about this yesterday. And I'm asking you again: Do you say -- do you say once more that you know nothing about that, that you don't know what happened? Is this your answer?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe I understand you. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In a simplified manner, what this reads here, about what you can read here, is your answer this didn't happen or I don't know if it happened?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this handing over of the Muslim population from Srebrenica on Zuti Most to the Serbian fighters in Bratunac? It is unclear to me. This is unclear to me. I don't know what this means. It is unclear, "To the Serbian fighters in Bratunac?" So literally, if I take it literally, then there are some Serbian fighters and somebody is being handed over to them. This is unclear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As this isn't clear to you, I will not continue asking questions about it. You spoke about this yesterday. I won't continue along these lines. Let us now take a look at Exhibit P01549. P01549. And while this is being put on the screen, let me say that this is an aerial photograph of the industrial zone in Potocari, taken on July 12th, 1995, at 1400 hours, and before we can see it I would like to ask you, on July 12th, 1995, around 1400 hours, you had a drink in Potocari; is that correct? Is it correct timewise?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can I just clarify that this image means it was taken around 1400 hours. That's what that squiggly mark means from the imagery provider, just to remind us all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm being told that on page 16, line 23 of the transcript, a part of the witness's testimony is not reflected correctly. So that -- what reads here, "Around 1400 hours he had a drink in Potocari," that was not my question. My question was whether the witness was there at that time. Can I ask the usher to provide the witness with the pencil in order for to us look at some of the details together?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How did this drink come into the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you are asking me, I perhaps may have taken a sip of water from my glass and that may have been the reason for it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: In the B/C/S there is only a one-letter difference in the words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see. It's a strange language, B/C/S. Yes, your next question. So we have this photo here which Mr. McCloskey has indicated shows the Potocari industrial area at around 1400 hours. So your question, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, did you get your bearings on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to disappoints you, but I really don't find any of this clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us try to go through this together, and we'll see if this works out. Do you see the white line in the middle, which is the road through the industrial zone in Potocari? If at the end of this line you can place the letter B?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, can you place the letter B on the right-hand side, in the -- on the bottom right-hand side corner? Please place the letter B there.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to the number 01 in red?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That would be the direction toward Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the upper corner, can you place the letter S for Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would this help you to orientate yourself? Do you see the markings and if you see the place where there are some people there, would that help you to get your bearings on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really apologise but I don't see any of what you've been telling me. Could you guide me more closely?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the central part of the photograph, do you see the black trace above which, in English, it is written "people"? The black trace which practically crosses the white line, do you see that? That's precisely in the centre of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said in English, and I don't speak English, "People."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the black trace cutting or running across the white line? It's right at the centre of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we -- can I place a dot for us to see whether we are speaking of the same thing? [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's put it more simply. Exactly. Where you put that dot right above it, there is a box and in it there are -- there is a word in English containing six letters, PEOPLE. That's where or the spot that Mr. Stojanovic is referring you to. Correct, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, let's proceed from there. Now your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, in order to be of assistance to the witness and to ourselves, let's pinpoint another location.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the lower left-hand corner, you see a building, and in front of it there are buses. It's a wider area which was referred to here as the bus station or the repair station and such like in Srebrenica or, rather, in Potocari. Can you orientate yourself now as to what was exactly photographed here?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really apologise but I cannot claim with certainty that it's all clear to me. It would be easier for me to draw for myself the position, the building, whatever you want me to. I can draw it. My movements throughout the day in metres and everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me try and help you both here. Now, if you divide the photo into four squares, the lower square or the last square in the bottom to the left, you see two arrows pointing up and they are shaded in a kind of a dirty pink colour. Next to those two arrows, there is a rectangular white box with a letter -- with a word in English, saying "trucks," I'll spell it for you as it is, TRUCKS. And an indicator, and an indicator there. This is the other spot that Mr. Stojanovic wants to you concentrate on. Now, do you wish to direct the witness to any other particular spot on this photo, Mr. Stojanovic? And I'll do it for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours -- Your Honour. I will try and see if we can work upon that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you help us now, having these landmarks in mind, and indicate with an X the place where you were or place a circle on roughly the place where you were on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise but this isn't clear to me at all. The photograph is not clear to me, and I was never able to orientate myself on any maps. I can try but I need someone's assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. There is another photo which shows a bigger -- the bigger area with the UN DutchBat compound clearly visible, and some -- and the factories nearby and some of the houses nearby. I think if we use that photo and then we zoom in and out as required, it will help the witness orient himself better, because this may -- I agree with him, it may be confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let us try it this way, then. Unless we are mistaken, this is a photograph from the collection we received from Mr. Ruez, P02103, P02103, photograph number 6 or 7, I'm not sure but I believe this allows us to have a better view. Perhaps that might help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If we see number 6, photo number 6,.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps then we can say that we won't be needing this photograph any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, you have to agree to using photo because I can't impose on you to use any particular photo, but I think it will be more helpful if he's shown photo number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you need to save this photo? I don't think there is any need for it because all we have there is --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, Your Honour. We won't be needing this photograph, and we won't be pursuing these questions since the witness obviously is having a hard time working on this. Your Honours, if we could have a look at the photograph number 7, we already used it while examining a witness here. This might assist the witness in getting his bearings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you will have before you a new photograph now, where the perspective will be different so that might help. Can this photograph help you to orient yourself and to establish the area of your movement on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've been trying to recognise --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I told you that in the bottom part of it was the direction to Srebrenica and at the top part, close to the UN base, was the direction to Zuti Most and Bratunac, would that assist you?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In that case, I'll ask you to take that pencil and to indicate the area where you were on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we just make sure he can orient himself because sometimes this is just hard for people to do. I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We can do that easily. Can you identify the UN DutchBat compound there on that photo and place an arrow next to it or an X next to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you go to the top right-hand corner, the extreme top right-hand corner, you see the road there. That road leads to where, to Srebrenica or to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If you can place the letter B where this part of the road toward Bratunac ends on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you tell me that Bratunac is in the top right-hand side corner, if you tell me that, because I don't recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I shouldn't be the one telling you that. We can only work this way if we agree and only if you're certain of it, can you place a marking?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Janjic, if you are in a car driving from Bratunac to Srebrenica, and you come to this road, you're driving in the direction of Srebrenica, would UN Dutch compound be to your left or to your right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Going from Bratunac, on the left-hand side, there is a large factory, in one of those there was a large UN base, and further down the road towards Srebrenica there is another factory on the left. They might even be physically next to each other, whether it was a battery manufacturing factory or cement, but they were both on the left-hand side as one goes towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So basically, if this is your position, and I put it to you that you are 100 per cent correct, then the road which you can barely see at the top right-hand corner of this photo is the road which takes you to where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I even indicated it that way, if you can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that is the road to Srebrenica or to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now it's clear to me. X is the road to Bratunac, and I'm referring to the last X that I placed. That's the road to Bratunac. Now it's clear to me, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you can change that last X into a B, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So the consequence of that is that the road that you see in the left-hand corner now, bottom of the photo, left, bottom left corner of the photo, that is the road to takes to you Srebrenica; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I may even mark it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So if you can put an S there, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You're being very kind and very cooperative. Now, Mr. Stojanovic, once you have more or less understood what is shown on this photo, would like you to mark with letters that you will explain to us your position on the 12th and on the 13th or on the 12th, we start with the 12th, Mr. Stojanovic? He is your witness so I wouldn't like to intervene more than I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I presume that there was some dynamics of it, that he was moving around, although in his statement he said that he was located at one site and then had to move a bit, but I'd like him to place a wider circle indicating the area of his movement on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will mark it in any event, but I just want to say that I know the side from which I came. This is something I can talk about, and I can note, but I don't know about the entire area of my movement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Use arrows and we will be able to understand what you are indicating.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The most part of the day, I spent from these crossroads and there is a factory here, I can put a letter next to it. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, try to do so.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a factory and this is a crossroads, and this is a -- there is a white circle, and my movement was hereabouts forward and backward and the like most of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please put the date the 12th of July above it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Put the date and your signature wherever you like, or your initials wherever you like. And for the record I'm just indicating that the witness has made some markings on the photo at between 35 -- at 40 minutes from the square indicating the UN base.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So if you could put the date 12th of July above it and in the lower right corner, please put today's date and your signature.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I can put both the 12th and the 13th there?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: 12th/13th July 1995, above these dots the Court has just explained to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I want to make sure that I am understanding the witness well. What you have marked on this map, is that the position -- your position more or less as it was on the 12th and on the 13th or only on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the place where I was both on the 12th and the 13th, one of the locations, but I'm also moved a little further toward Bratunac and I can mark it. But not further than that, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Then concentrate on one of the corners and put today's date, please. Today is the 21st. And your signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks] As far as I understood, I'm supposed to put both the 12th and the 13th as dates above those dots.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead. Do that. Just put 12 plus 13, Juli.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And, please now mark on this photograph, by a circle, the area where you saw most of the soldiers of the DutchBat on the 12th and the 13th, on this road.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot do that. What do you mean most of the soldiers? I don't know how many they were. I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll try to be more specific. Can you mark the area where you saw the members of the DutchBat moving?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we did it in blue it might help.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no problem with that. It may be a good idea.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On both days, I saw UNPROFOR members. They were moving along the road where I could see them. They were reaching the imaginary ramp. They brought water, they carried people on stretchers. That's what I saw of them. And they were present on those two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Just mark their position on the map, please, in blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The ramp, as you call it.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] I am marking the area that I could see next to me and a little further, and I think that this imaginary ramp was hereabouts, it cannot be seen clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree with me when I say that the members of the civilian police that you mentioned on those days were at the places marked in blue where you said the ramp was?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand -- or I don't agree that I said members of the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Members of the Special Police, as you called them, or the specials, were they at the places that you marked as the position of the ramp?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the Special Police, I mentioned the name of one of its members, and I mentioned the activities of the other members of the Special Police from the ramp to my area of movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did the officer who you mentioned by name, according to what you saw, was by the ramp as it is marked here?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him there, and I saluted him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, could you help us and say whether the able-bodied men who were separated, according to what you saw, were taken to the same house on the 12th and the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained that in detail too. On the first day, I didn't mention the house. It was a yard and garden. And I assumed that some were taken to the house too. And I added that along the road, now having a map I could even tell where, maybe at the points 12, 13, and even 07 in the -- as shown on the map, were along the road, on the meadow, and I think I could mark the position of that building or facility, as you called it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I would like you to do that. This was going to be my next question but let's proceed your way. Do mark it and then I will ask my question.

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking from the right, from the direction of Bratunac, close to this crossroads, marked with the numbers 12 and 13, there is a small road or path to the right next to the figure 12 in the image, and in the immediate vicinity, there is a -- there is a gate which is the entrance to that facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would first like to ask you whether that was the place, the place of assembly both on the 12th and 13th?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were there, and I also added some information about the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will finish with this photograph and it is both dated and signed, so that I can -- so that we can thank both you and the usher and save this photograph. Thank you for your assistance. During those two days, did you hear comments from the members of the military or the police that there was a list of war criminals with which the command of the 1st Bratunac Brigade was familiar and that an investigation was to be launched whether someone from that list was among the persons in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was some speculation, there were rumours, but I had never heard anyone ordering that, issuing such an order. There were rumours about that, but I don't know whether that's important.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now together look at Exhibit 4D00015, page 1 of both the B/C/S and English versions, and you will now see on your screen that document. I would like to ask you one question. You will see in front of you a document entitled, "The List of War Criminals Known to the Command of the 1st Light Infantry Brigade who Have Committed War Crimes in the Areas of the Municipalities," and they are stated." You said that people spoke about that and my question is whether you have heard about the existence of such a list at any time, and was it -- and whether it was used in the investigation that was launched?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never heard of the existence of a list, and I -- this is also the first time I've heard that an investigation was conducted. This is news to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You know nothing about that?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You have already spoken about buses leaving from Potocari toward Bratunac. The number of buses that you mentioned, was it -- did those buses come at once or did they come in several waves or from time to time? Is it from time to time that the people were being taken away?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered this question at least three times yesterday. If you want, I can answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll be more precise. You spoke about the 12th, and you were more precise from 10 to 1500 [as interpreted], and you also mentioned the evening hours. Now I'll ask you about the 13th. You also mentioned the numbers. Is -- so now my question is, on the 13th, did the buses come at once, or did they come in waves?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry but with we may want to clarify the 10 to 1500. I'm not sure that's what he meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. He did clarify yesterday, I think, but -- and precisely because of the same figures. So yesterday when we spoke about these numbers, you specified that they were from 10 to 15. Is that what you mean, Mr. Stojanovic? And not -- we were not talking of thousands?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, exactly, Your Honours. That's what I said, 10 to 15. I believe this is only a problem with the transcript. The witness and I understand each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So go ahead, if you can answer the question, Mr. Janjic, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So on the second day, you asked whether they were leaving in groups. So not as on the first day, 10 to 15. I spoke about this yesterday. We, during the day, together with the other vehicles, with the trucks, with the women, they were leaving separately. I mean, the men and the women were separated, to put it clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not clear. Mr. Stojanovic, can you repeat your question and cut it in different questions so that we know what we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, will you agree with me when I say that on the second day, the 13th of July, the transportation of the able-bodied men did not take place at once, but on several occasions during that day, July the 13th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And to finish my question, when you arrived on the 13th of July, to continue carrying out your assignment, what time of day was it?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the morning, as I said, and earlier than on the first day. After coming from the Fontana, I cannot state to you precisely but it was earlier than on the first day. Around 10.00 or before 10.00, but now this -- this -- the hour is a conjecture. Anyway, it was in the morning and earlier than on the first day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this just to understand, because I know what you were doing. Is it possible that the buses were already or had already been leaving before you arrived there and before you started counting?

utterances.speaker: MILE JANJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any buses on the way. They may have left during the night, maybe, maybe not. I never saw them so I cannot say whether they had left before I arrived there, and I believe Colonel Jankovic, who came on the next day after me, how that went, who organised that, in whose presence, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. No more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. There are no further cross-examinations. Do you wish to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. Janjic, we haven't got any further questions for you, which means that we've made it. You're free to go. You've finished your testimony. Our staff will assist you. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, my colleagues, Judge Kwon, Judge Prost, Judge Stole, I would like to thank you for having come over to give testimony, and we also wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And I thank everybody present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We will have the break now, and we'll do the documents, the exhibits, after the break, Mr. McCloskey, is that okay with you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a 25 minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We have 65 ter number 2963, that previous testimony in the Blagojevic case of this witness. This witness also identified two still photographs, and they come from a book of photographs that has been marked for identification, not yet that book has not yet been offered into evidence. Tomasz Blaszczyk will be testifying about that entire book, and so we are fine on just waiting until we get to Mr. Blaszczyk on that book to offer that book into evidence or these photographs individually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But in the meantime, he's put his markings on these two photos and signed, so I think they ought to be given --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Actually, anything that he's marked I think should come into evidence independently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Whether it's admitted or marked for identification purposes is another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have no objection to anything that he's marked should come in as evidence independently of the book, because it really is independent of the ID book, but he didn't mark anything for us I'm told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not for you but he did mark both for Mr. Stojanovic -- I think he marked for Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. And I won't have any objection to any of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Otherwise, apart from 65 ter 2963, do you have any other documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, yes, do I. And I would call the Court's attention to the reference of Mr. Stojanovic made of the statement of facts Momir Nikolic made pursuant to his plea agreement and guilty plea which is in evidence in full. And Mr. Stojanovic challenged some of the factual assertions by Mr. Nikolic in that, at length, with this witness. As such, I would like to offer, under Rule 94, I would like to offer Mr. Nikolic's guilty plea of 6 and 7th May 2003, and the acceptance of that plea by the Court, as a judicial notice of a fact of common knowledge or as evidence to rebut the implications and the evidence put forward through this witness. And this is potentially complex area which we will certainly be able to provide the Court written material on, if you so choose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there any objection? Yes, don't rush, take it one after the other. Yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this judicial notice only takes into account the fact Momir Nikolic made a plea agreement and a guilty plea. There I see no objection to this if that's the only thing. However, regarding the accuracy of the facts that are noted in the statement of facts and in the plea agreement, there, I do not -- I objected to this being tendered as notorious facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I provide it to the Court for any weight it should be allowed, that it should feel it should give. But for the truth of the matter asserted in it, but of course if you wish to set it aside and not give it any value that's your discretion. So I don't offer it as the God's honest truth and only the truth, but we do offer it as a -- as to go to the credibility of those statements of facts which have been challenged by Mr. Stojanovic. And I will recall to the Court that this statement of facts was initially introduced by Mr. Stojanovic. This is not something the Prosecution is piggy backing on to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He didn't introduce the whole document. He introduced part of that document with this witness and asked some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The document was already in -- it's my understanding that the entire document was already into evidence under Major Boering as introduced by the Borovcanin team many months ago. That's what I was referring to. And he's now -- he's now -- and I believe he attacked it through Major Boering, though I don't remember, but he certainly attacked it through this witness, and so I think he has opened the door to me being able to rebut that with the admissions of Momir Nikolic, his guilty plea the acceptance of that by the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's check what was admitted with Major Boering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Then -- okay. So I think the position is very simple. If you wish to tender -- or if you wish to move before the Trial Chamber, for the taking of judicial notice of a documentary evidence from the Momir Nikolic proceedings, pursuant to Rule 94, we suggest that you do so in writing, by means of an ad hoc motion, and then everyone will have an opportunity to discuss that and it will also give us the opportunity to decide after hearing your submissions, your respective submissions. As regards to the use made today of parts of that document by Mr. Stojanovic, I think we'll wait to see what Mr. Stojanovic has in mind, and then we see. But let's conclude on your list, the Prosecution list. His previous testimony in Blagojevic. What else?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's it, Mr. President, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Now, Defence teams, who wishes to tender any document? Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, only P113, the report of Colonel Jankovic of July 13th 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection from the other Defence teams? None. So admitted. Yours is also admitted, Mr. McCloskey. Any other Defence team would like to tender any document? Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we move that the marked diagram be admitted, 4D.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we will be of course responding to the filing by the Prosecution in writing concerning the judicial notice of the facts that are just being asked to be admitted. Let me repeat: 4DIC 191.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. The two things are different. What Mr. McCloskey is seeking is completely different from the possible tendering on your part of either the whole document which is already in the records or the part from that document which you made use of. But anyway I'm not going to interfere with that. If you wish to tender it, you tender it. If you don't wish to tender it, we stop there and proceed with the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, the answer is we are not tendering it. We are mindful of the fact that the statement is already in -- it's already in evidence and it's marked 4D00016.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So is there any objection to the other document, the photo that has been marked?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That is admitted. No further documents, I take it? Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So is the next witness ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No -- I just want a confirmation that there are no protective measures involved?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour, but I think that the witness should receive a caution, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Jovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I wish to welcome you to this trial.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where you are about to start giving evidence. I don't think we will finish with you today, but we'll make our best and make sure that we will finish with your testimony tomorrow. Before you start, however, there is a solemn procedure that we need to follow. You need to give us your undertaking, your word, that you will be testifying the truth, and for that purpose, you're required to make the solemn declaration that is contained in the text that is being handed to you by Madam Usher. Read it out aloud, please, and that will be your undertaking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please make yourself comfortable. And welcome once more. I'll briefly, very briefly, explain to you what's going to happen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're going to be asked several questions first by Mr. Nicholls for the Office of the Prosecutor and subsequently by the various Defence teams which you have to your right. In the course of the questions that will be put to you, there could be a possibility - I'm not saying that this will happen - but there could be a possibility of questions put to you, being put to you, which, if answered truthfully by you, could possibly expose you to criminal proceedings later on. Now, as in most countries, we have a provision in our law which protects the witness from self-incrimination, which means that if such a question is put to you, and if you believe that by answering truthfully you would expose yourself to criminal proceedings, then you can ask us, the four judges here, to consider exempting you from answering such questions. I told you you had a right, but it's not an absolute right. It's a limited right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the sense that we can either accede to your request, or we can disagree with you completely and compel you to answer such questions. If we do compel to you answer such questions, then there is a further right that you enjoy, namely that provided that your answer is truthful, whatever you state here in answering such questions cannot be made use of in any proceedings that might be taken against you. That is a guarantee that our law, our rules, provide you with. Have I made myself clear? Have you understood what I tried to explain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's very good. That paves the way for the commencement of your testimony. Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber your full name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Jovic, 26th of July 1959, Zvornik, Rocevici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you would describe your ethnicity as that you are a Bosnian Serb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you tell us what your present job is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I am a private businessman, haulier.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And where were you born? You said that, excuse me, Rocevic. Where do you live now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I live in Rocevic, and I am registered in the Osmace municipality. I have been some seven or eight years ago because I had some tax benefits beforehand. Now it's all the same. I live in Rocevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. I want to start asking you some questions now about 1995. In July 1995, can you tell us what your rank and position was in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hold any rank. I was the driver for the commander of the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat the name, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you tell us the name of the commander, please? It wasn't picked up.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Sreco Acimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how long had you been Commander Acimovic's driver? When did you start driving for him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: As of March of 1993, I guess. I don't recall exactly, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And in July 1995, where were you living? Where was your family home when you weren't on duty?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: In the house at Rocevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And your house in Rocevic, how far is that from the school in Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Around 200 metres, more or less, around 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And do you recall that the first time I met you was on the 30th of June 2007, and on that day you gave a tape-recorded interview to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when you arrived here in The Hague, were you given an opportunity to review the transcript of your interview with the assistance of an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you have any changes or alterations to your interview or do you stand by that statement you gave to us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: As far as my statement is concerned, I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And last question on this topic, before you met with me on the 30th of June, had you given an interview to investigators for the Defence in this case?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. I want to ask you now some more questions about July 1995, specifically concerning the Rocevic area. During this time, in the days following the fall of Srebrenica or the Srebrenica campaign, did you become aware of any Muslim prisoners being held in the Rocevic area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I had heard of it on the eve of the execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Tell me -- tell me what you heard about prisoners in Rocevic. Where were they held?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I was outside the command where I was all the time, either at the back of the building or in front of it, when a young man came up who was a member, a soldier, of our battalion, who had been visiting someone or I don't know what, in Rocevic. He passed by the reception area and said that Muslims, prisoners, had been brought over to the hall at Rocevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And is that the hall of the school in Rocevic, the gym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. What else did he tell you about what was going on at the school? What did you hear was going on at the school where the prisoners were held?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that there were dead among them, and that Joco Stojanovic, I don't know who called him or ordered him anything, that he came to take them away by tractor. What he did and how, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to be clear, I sometimes have to ask follow-up questions even though you are answering well. Are these dead Serbs or Muslims that were taken away by tractor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they must have been Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you hear about whether any -- excuse me -- Serb civilians had been hurt or wounded at this time, around the school?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you describe that, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I heard that during either the killing of the Muslims or, I don't know when, the wife of Petko Tanaskovic was wounded, who is also some 200 metres away from the school. She was wounded in her arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And just last question or two on this topic, did you hear how many Muslims had been killed at the school in Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you go to the school yourself --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you, whether it was the evening before the executions or on the day of the executions or what, on the eve of the executions?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me try to make that clearer. When you first heard -- on the day that the wife of Petko Tanaskovic was wounded, did you hear how many Muslims had been killed that day? Or another way of saying it, how many Muslims were taken away on the tractor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, that day, when you heard this information, did you personally go to Rocevic school that same day that you heard about this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The next day did you go anywhere from the command of the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Where did you go on the following day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: We woke up in the morning, had breakfast, I was in front of the command where my post was. I believe I was in the front of the command, I don't know exactly. Sreco Acimovic called me and asked me to drive him. I asked him where. He told me, "You should go towards Kozluk."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And then where did you go? Please tell us where you went with Acimovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: When we arrived, we continued our journey to Rocevic, in front -- we stopped in front of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Approximately what time did you arrive at the school in Rocevic that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, between 10.00 or 11.00. I'm not sure. I never had a watch on me, just to tell you that. It was a general conundrum and I don't know who told Sreco Acimovic that we should go to Rocevic. I only know that he ordered me to take him down there and that we went to the school in Rocevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. It's not a huge point but in your interview you said between 11.00 and noon. Does that help you remember? Which do you think is more accurate, 10.00 to 11.00 or 11.00 to noon when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, around that time. It's quite possible 11.00, 12.00 noon. I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like you to describe in your own words to the Trial Chamber, if you could, what you saw at the school when you arrived there with Acimovic? What was the scene there? What did you see going on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: As we arrived and entered the school yard, to the left there was an UNPROFOR APC. I parked my car next to the APC, between the two buildings, where there was a shade. From there, we went directly into the school. The school was unlocked. Sreco asked that the door to an office be opened where there was a phone line. I can't tell you whether there was the school secretary there or probably I went to fetch the school secretary to get the keys in order to open the door to the office where there were phones. And that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. What's the name of the school secretary that you're referring to? Do you remember his name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I do, Boro Lakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The APC, can you describe that, what colour it was, which unit or organisation it belonged to, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I only know that it was white in colour. Whose it was I don't know. I don't know which army it belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you see any VRS soldiers or military police or any other military personnel around the school when you arrived with Mr. Acimovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you describe how many of these soldiers or military police you saw?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in front of the gym, perhaps up to ten, but there were some of them in front of the gym and behind the school, perhaps some 15 to 20 of them. I don't know. This wasn't important to me. I didn't go counting them and nobody told me to record that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I realise you weren't at that time thinking would you have to remember the precise number, were these -- which unit did these men belong to, who were around the school and in front of the gym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: There was talk that they belonged to the Bratunac Brigade. I didn't know them. Which means that they weren't part of our brigade, but people said that they belonged to the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Who said they belonged to the Bratunac Brigade? Which people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: It may have been Sreco or someone who said that they belonged to the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And were these MPs or ordinary soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: They were MPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
