utterances.text: All right. What happened after you got the keys to -- from Boro Lakic? What happened next?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Sreco Acimovic entered the office. I saw no one, no soldier, no officer, anyone. I stayed in the hall way, some 20 metres from the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You didn't go into the office or did you go into the office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And how long did you stay in the hallway or did you go somewhere else after a while?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I stayed for a short while. In the meantime Sreco came out and I asked him, since the campaign lasted for a number of days, I was dirty and all, and as my house was nearby, I asked him for permission to go to my home to change and wash quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now before --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: And this took me about 40 minutes or an hour, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: My absence, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, before you went home, did you see any prisoners personally? I mean, did you see any prisoners in the school or in the gym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When I left to go home, I couldn't believe that this was taking place there in our village. I went to the gym and took a look. A quarter maybe, in fact, a third, was full of soldiers and civilians who were sitting on the floor of the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you about how sure you are about that gym being a third full. If could you think about it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: It seemed to me at first glance.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: So a quarter almost was empty or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So if a quarter of the gym was empty, perhaps then the gym was three-quarters full; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes. I didn't express myself so well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When you went home, did you go home alone or did you go with anybody?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I went alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what -- what did you do after that time that you were at home? Where did you go next when you left your house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: After my bath and having changed, I returned to the school. I was in front of the school as agreed with Sreco. When I came up to the school, I saw a military jeep, a Campagnola on the road in front school, not on the sports ground but on the road. And then I saw Sreco with some man. They were talking, and I went to the car and sat in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How far away were you when you saw Sreco Acimovic speaking with this other man?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: About 30 metres, where my car was, and they were standing in front of the goal on the soccer pitch, and I was standing by the building, so we would have been some 30 metres apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you hear what they were talking about, Sreco and this other man?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: As best you can, describe the appearance of the man you're referring to that you saw Sreco Acimovic talking to 30 metres away? What did he look like?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he was of a powerful stature like Sreco. I don't know if he was a little shorter or taller than Sreco. He was wearing a military uniform with no ranks and no uniform hat. He did have -- he had no weapons and he didn't belong to the Zvornik Brigade. I didn't know him. I would have known him if he belonged to the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember anything else about the appearance of this man?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing else. He was shaven, with a round face, rather a big man, you would say. As I said about your colleague when you were hearing me in Kozluk or -- in fact, I don't remember who said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And just to be clear there, you're referring to my colleague, Tomasz Blaszczyk, that you said that they were about the same size; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think so. I don't really remember who said it. Maybe you did, or I.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We can go over that later if we need to. What happened next after you saw Mr. Acimovic talking to this man?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, nothing much. When that man left in his jeep, Acimovic called me and said that I should go to see Draskovic, whose brother had been killed early on in the war, but Kula or Liplje, three or four of them were killed there and their bodies were never found. So he sent me over to that man, to ask him whether he would be -- he would want to come and execute, but when he mentioned the execution, the firing, to the extent possible, I opposed him and I said to him, "Sreco, is that more normal? What are you doing, man?" And he answered, "We have to do that. It's an order, the order must be carried out." And that's it. And he sent me over to Draskovic, and I went over to Draskovic's house which was about a kilometre and a half or two away and asked him, I said to him that Sreco had sent me to ask him whether he would like to come and execute the people from Srebrenica. Sreco probably reckoned that Draskovic had lost a brother and that he might want to take vengeance but Draskovic didn't want to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Did Sreco Acimovic tell you what he had been discussing with that man you saw him talking to in any detail? Did he tell you what they had been talking about or how long they had been talking?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You asked more than one question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you split it into two parts, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did -- it's the same question, but I'll split it up. Did Sreco Acimovic tell you what he'd been discussing with that man you saw him with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did he tell you how long he had been with that man talking while you'd been in your home?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I was away for about 40 minutes or 50, up to an hour, I don't know exactly. Whether they had been in the school before that, I don't know, but when I returned I saw them in front -- standing in front of the goal on the soccer pitch. The man wore a uniform. He was well shaven. He didn't -- I didn't see any weapons on his person. He wasn't wearing ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What happened after you came back from Draskovic's house? Coming back now to after you'd been sent to get this man to help execute the prisoners and he refused, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, nothing. I think that the truck, the battalion's Mercedes driven by Veljko Ivanovic, was already there, waiting, and the decision was taken. Sreco certainly wouldn't have taken that decision by himself if he hadn't been ordered to. But from whom that order came, he knows best. He said that we had to go to Kozluk because there the execution would take place. And before the war he also transported gravel from that place. It was a gravel pit. And there was an elderly man who didn't know where that was, that Veljko Ivanovic. As I was a private entrepreneur before the war, I knew exactly where that was and that's why I went there with Veljko in his truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Let me go back and ask you some questions about what you've just said. Were you ordered to go with Veljko Ivanovic in the truck and show him the place in Kozluk or was that something that you came up with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't ask that --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Not by myself. It was -- I was ordered to go there because Veljko didn't know the place, and I had transported gravel from the place, so I was sent there with him to show him the way of the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell me, describe for the Court, how the prisoners were transported out of the school and to Kozluk? Describe that, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: They were -- they were in trucks, in the back of trucks, and military police, two or three, were with them there or four at the most, and that's how they were transported.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you tell -- first of all, this truck, the Mercedes, how big is that truck? Can you describe it, please? The battalion's Mercedes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: It's a smaller Mercedes, with a tarpaulin, able to carry some five to seven tonnes, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you remember, approximately how many prisoners were put in the back of the Mercedes truck on the first trip?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't in the back and I didn't count, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you describe, as best you can, where you went to in Kozluk with Veljko Ivanovic in his truck and with the prisoners? Where did the truck stop?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Rocevic-Kozluk, that's six kilometres, and the gravel pit is about three kilometres away from Kozluk, and the road is very bad. I was surprised myself because I remember what it looked like before, but five years later, it was all overgrown, it was even hard to recognise. We drove the truck as far as we could get, and Veljko turned around and there, they were unloaded, and they were taken away, but I didn't see what happened later. They must have been shot there. But I didn't witness that. I only accompanied Veljko to show him the way. And there, there were the pits from which gravel and sand had been dug out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who unloaded the prisoners from the truck, when they arrived at that location in Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: The military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Is that military police who accompanied the truck from Rocevic school or were there military police already there waiting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody was there waiting. It was the military police who had been in Rocevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then what did you and Veljko Ivanovic do after the prisoners had been taken off the truck? What happened next?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: We returned to Rocevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then what happened? What did you do next when you got back to Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: When I returned to Rocevic, Sreco Acimovic -- you could say that he ordered me to fetch the truck from Mico Stanojevic, who -- whose truck was requisitioned for the military, and I went there to Mico Stanojevic's house which was some -- a kilometre and a half away, to inform him of Sreco's order. So I got to his house, I asked for Mico Stanojevic, his wife came out, and his mother. I said to them that Sreco had sent me for Mico. Whether there had been a telephone conversation before, I don't know, but he sent me to fetch the truck. His mother came out and said, no, you can't take the truck. And his wife also said I couldn't. And the truck was or rather belonged to Mico's relative, and it was to be used to transport soldiers. And that guy lives in -- close to Padine and Sreco then said, "We'll go there together." And we drove there in my car. And again, Mico's mother and wife came out who again said that they wouldn't give us the truck, but Sreco used his authority because he was a battalion commander, and he had to be respected. He didn't use force but he sternly ordered them to give us the keys to the truck. I had a truck before the war, and I sold it in 1991, so I could drive any truck. So I took the truck and Sreco returned to Rocevic in my car. And Sreco -- and I continued as ordered by Sreco to take soldiers to Kozluk. Two or three times I took soldiers there. It was a smaller truck. Maybe -- it could hold some ten prisoners or so at a time, and the soldiers securing those civilians and prisoners, Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, the first -- I'm going to come back to this, but the first trip that you took with Veljko, where you -- when the prisoners were loaded, taken to Kozluk and taken down that difficult road, unloaded and then you returned, how long did that whole trip take, round trip? How long was that process, the entire first --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Not less than an hour, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Because from Kozluk, there were three kilometres to the gravel pit on a bad road which was not -- had not been maintained for five years, so it was even difficult to walk on that road, let alone drive a truck on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. When you came back -- just to be clear -- and you got the second truck, what was that truck going to be used for, the truck which you and Sreco went and were able to persuade Mico Stanojevic's mother and wife to give to you, what was that truck for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: It was used for the same purpose as Veljko's truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Transporting prisoners to Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, approximately how many round trips did you make, taking prisoners to Kozluk, using Stanojevic's truck?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I said a little while ago two to three times. I don't remember exactly. So two times at least, up to three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And if you know, how many trips did Veljko Ivanovic make with his truck, the Mercedes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. You'd have to ask him. (redacted). Veljko was nervous on that day, and I don't know how he was able to drive because he was ill. He was ill even before the war but especially in such a situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we go into private session for one moment, please, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, were there any other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes, we are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: As best you remember, were there any other trucks used besides the two you've already talked about? Any other trucks that you saw that day being used to transport prisoners from the Rocevic school to Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I saw that Milivoje Lazarevic also drove a load, if you pardon the expression, a truck load. I don't really remember. When I was asked by the Nikolic Defence, I'm not sure, whether I remember that there was Djoko Nikolic, I really can't remember. I can't remember whether that man was there with a truck. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, how long did this entire operation, I'll call it, take? How long was it until all the prisoners were transported out of the school and had been taken to the execution site?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: It started late because there was expectation that it wouldn't begin. Nobody was for that. I said to Sreco right away that it shouldn't be done but he received an order, I don't know from whom, he knows that, and the -- it lasted from 2.00 or 3.00 until -- I was there until 6.00 or 7.00 when Mico took over the truck from me. I don't know exactly. I'm not sure about the times. But thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: After Mico Stanojevic took over the truck from you, did he drive any prisoners from the school? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: You'd have to ask him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, after the last prisoners had been taken away from the school, what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't stay until the end. When I gave the keys, that is when I handed over the truck, to Mico Stanojevic, Sreco ordered me to take some sandwiches and juice and mineral water to another place, and then I went home because he didn't tell me to return. So it would have been around 5.00 or 6.00 when Sreco sent me away. And having delivered those sandwiches and mineral water and juice, I didn't go to see those soldiers there and I didn't return to the school. I don't know how long it all lasted and what time it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What time did you actually get home that night or that evening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps at around 7.30 or 8.00. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I found one slip in translation. The witness said that he brought mineral water and juices and sandwiches to the soldiers. Not -- it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're maintaining that he said that he took.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then it doesn't tally with the transcript. Mr. Jovic, what did do you with the sandwiches, mineral water and the juice? What did you do with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I handed the truck over to Mico Stanojevic, I came to the school and to Sreco, who told me to take the sandwiches and to drop by a store in Kozluk to buy some mineral water and juices and that the battalion would sort that out, and I took this down to those soldiers and the first soldiers I came across I gave them the goods.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And which soldiers are these that you're bringing the juice and the food to? The mineral water and juices?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: When I first left with Veljko, there was only the military police there. When I arrived with Mico Stanojevic's truck, there was already a larger presence of the army, together with the military police, and I mean the presence of the army that was unknown to me. They weren't from the 2nd Battalion, I don't know where they were from. They were unknown to me. There were soldiers who were not members of the 2nd Battalion who were from Kozluk but they were assigned to all manner of battalions. Although I was a haulier, it was the first time at Branjevo and now in the streets of Zvornik I meet some people for the first time although I've been living there for a long time. Whether they were members of the 2nd Battalion, and I didn't know them, or whether they were sent from outside, from some other battalion or brigade, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say you meet some people, when you meet some people in Zvornik, you're talking there about people who were -- who are you talking about there? People -- you just said in your answer sometimes you meet people for the first time in the streets of Zvornik, and you don't know which units they were from. Are you -- which people are you talking about? Why -- when you talk about meeting people in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: What I want to say is that in Kozluk, which is a Muslim place, Muslims who lived there were moved out, and there were people moved in from Tuzla, Zivinice, Zenica, half of Bosnia was in Kozluk, and all these people were assigned to all the different units in the Zvornik Brigade and outside the Zvornik Brigade, and even now, when I move about the town, I meet some people for the first time. So I don't know these people even today, let alone at that time we are discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. But were any of these people who were present at Kozluk, at the execution site? People from Zenica and elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I don't know. I don't know. I can't really speculate about that. I didn't see any of the people I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me ask you about this because you've -- because it's come up, you've brought it up. In your statement, you talked about how now even after 15 years sometimes when you transport construction material to people from Zenica or other places, some of them tell you that they were there, also there, at Kozluk. Can you tell me what you were referring to there? Did you meet people who had also been at Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, no. Those were people residing in Kozluk at the time who were assigned throughout the Zvornik Brigade. I didn't see them there. What I meant was that they were occupying Muslim houses and were assigned to all the different parts of the Zvornik Brigade. I don't know now in terms of percentage of our people who were in our battalion. Of course, there were more in the entire battalion. Maybe Mr. Pandurevic knows, the battalion has some 500 to 600 people. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Was Sreco Acimovic at the school in Rocevic the whole day, as far as you could see, or did he go away at some point?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this was between five and six hours that he was there for sure. After that, I didn't talk to him, I didn't see him. I went home. I don't know where he went. It was only the next day that I went to Malesic, to the command. Nobody had been asking for me in the meantime or anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me just ask you this question, I'm sorry you may have answered this but I missed it, when you're bringing the juice and the mineral water to the soldiers, is that soldiers at the school or soldiers at the execution site in Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: At the execution site, but they were outside of that site. They were waiting for the buses. They couldn't come to that site itself, to the pit itself, because it was overgrown by vegetation, and the first soldiers I came across and saw, I stopped, took the sandwiches, mineral water and juice out of the boot, gave it to them and left. After that, I didn't call Sreco, he didn't call me. I never carried a Motorola, I wasn't the commander of a single squad, platoon or a company. I was only serving the army -- service, I was providing a service to the army. I couldn't make any decisions or order anyone anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Nothing else at this time. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who is going first? Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will have a break in about 20 minutes time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I can begin, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Jovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I have less questions than expected to ask you. Many of the questions I intended to ask were already asked by my colleague, but in any event I will still go through the events as they unfolded. I think it will be easier for you to understand each of the questions I'm going to ask you. Do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. If I don't understand you, I will tell you so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. First starting with the fact that you were the driver of Sreco Acimovic, can you confirm that you were a member of the command of the 2nd Battalion in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: The driver of the commander of the 2nd Battalion, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So the place where you stayed at that time was at the command of the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And in July of 1995, when you were driving Sreco Acimovic, you were using your own vehicle and that was a Mercedes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And my fuel too. My car, my fuel, which cost 15.000 German marks at the time. 100 litres of fuel a month costing 500 German marks that I paid for. I sold a new truck in 1991 which I wouldn't have saved my head unless I worked for the command. That's why Sreco admitted me as a driver to help me have the job.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And one of the reasons you got into this agreement was because you had a problem with your spine and your leg. You had water in your knee, I believe; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: In 1993, at Viska Glavica, in the direction of Zeca [phoen] Kosa, Kovacvici, Mr. Pandurevic knows the area, I was driving a tractor, with a bucket. It was raining and snowing. There were Pinzgauers and Lada Nivas with chains that weren't unable to reach the front lines to collect the wounded and the dead. I drove them all the way to the medical corps. It would so happen that I would drive a dead person in the bucket and two soldiers would hold him, and a Muslim howitzer shell would land two metres away from me, wounding one of the soldiers in the bucket, and you know what a Pinzgauer with chains on is. What sort of terrain it can -- can be trafficable for it, but that sort of terrain was not trafficable for that vehicle. And I've had problems with my spine. And up until 1992, 1993, I had to drink 600-millimetre [as interpreted] prophines in the mornings and evenings, pain killers to endure this. Nobody believed me, not even the doctors. In 1993, I was able to drive a tractor in one of the actions, and I get water in my knee at the start of the action. I went to Zvornik to the hospital to Vucetic who said that water had to be extracted from my knee, but that what was required were more expensive injections that my knee had to be injected with in order to prevent further forming of any water. My wife had an uncle in Belgrade and I spoke to him and he said, "Well, if you can get a prescription, if not all the same, you have to come to Belgrade to the orthopaedic ward there." I went there to my wife's uncle, who -- well, I went there without having to pay for anything. I went to the main orthopaedic specialist there, probably all of you know Lepa Brena the singer and Bobo Zivojinovic the tennis player, and I was treated by that orthopaedic doctor who treated the tennis player, and I had this -- I had this plaster that I had to wear and I received tablets in Belgrade, I had to report to Dr. Vucetic to extend my sick leave. But he told me that the tablets I was prescribed with would never assist anyone with anything and they wouldn't help me either. So I had to stay put for 20 days resting, and even to this day my knee has not been giving me any trouble but my spine has been giving me trouble, and I'm limping on my right foot because the three fingers on my right foot, the three toes on my right foot are causing me trouble and I can't stand on them. And all of this trouble emerged during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And luckily by using your car and paying for that fuel, you managed to stay at the 2nd Battalion command, and you avoided going back to the trenches; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I was supposed to go back because I was supposed to appear before a commission once the plaster was taken off. I was supposed to appear before a commission. However, Sreco met me on one of these occasions I was going back from a medical checkup. He had known me from before. He knew that I was a private haulier and that I had to sell my truck in 1991 for 20.000 German marks. He knew that I had some money on the side, some savings, so he told me, rather than ending up somewhere, you should come to my command, use your Lada, and be our driver for the battalion. This way, you can take care of your health, and you can avoid being engaged in fighting the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you for sharing this with us. Now, at the 2nd Battalion command, I take it that you were sleeping in a house which was by the command but you did not sleep in the command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I slept in the rear, because Sreco was a great man. None of the soldiers could sleep at the command. Only those who were desk officers, who worked in the moral guidance sector, and those higher up, they were able to sleep at the command. We, the ordinary soldiers, had to sleep in the rear in some homes, in very bad conditions, with no bathroom facilities of any sort. We were eating directly from the pots in the kitchen, whereas Sreco had a cook who brought him food as if he was in a hotel, and to some others who were members of the command, because they were the higher ups. They were powerful people at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, this man that came to -- by the command to the -- the first one to share the information concerning the prisoners taken in the Rocevic school, you don't know the name of this man, do you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: He didn't share his opinion with me. It was by happenstance that I was at the gate. In front of the command, there was the gate and that's where we were. We were always at the ready to be dispatched somewhere. At some point, I was assigned to go to Baljkovica as an aide, perhaps some five platoons from the 2nd Battalion went to Baljkovica. Sreco's cousin, who was also sent to Baljkovica, never came back. That man, he was a member of the 2nd Battalion. I don't know his name although I know him by sight. He was born in Malesic and he was married in Rocevic, and he happened to come at that point, but I don't know who told this to Sreco at the command, whether it came by telegraph or whether it was the courier, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, that this man, when he gave that information, you made -- you mentioned in your statement or your -- during your interview that the soldiers at the school who were guarding the prisoners, that they were drunk? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when that man came by the command, my understanding is that this took place in the evening or at dusk; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was at dusk, just before night fall. He probably had to get to the front line before dark. Since his house is situated practically at the front line in Malesic, his family must have been in Rocevic and he went to visit them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And that night, the night that this man came by the battalion, I take it that you slept in that house by the command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you did not hear or see anything special that night that you recall, something -- anything special happened that night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No, nothing. I simply went to sleep and you're waiting at the command. One could still hear gunfire from Baljkovica all the way in front of the lines of our 2nd Battalion, and I'm sure that Mr. Pandurevic knows this better. He's familiar with the terrain, that is. I don't know if he heard this or not. I did. The gunfire, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: If I look at -- you testified earlier that you parked your car between two buildings behind the school, and my understanding is that you immediately entered the school at that time with Sreco Acimovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: That's not correct. Not behind the school. In front of the school. There were two residential buildings in front of the school, and I parked my vehicle right next the APC, close to trees, since it was quite warm, the weather, that's where I parked the car, in the shade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Maybe it's my question that was not clear enough. After parking the car, you went directly into the school with Sreco Acimovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you did not meet anybody outside, a high-ranking officer, before going into the school?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. And when you went inside the school, Sreco Acimovic went into one of those offices and you stayed in the hallway, and just to confirm, the distance about where you were from where Acimovic was, that office, is about 20 metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly that much. It's quite a long school hallway. I didn't have access to the command in Malesic, and even less would I have that here. Yes, I was at least 20 to 30 metres away from the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: You mentioned that you never went into that office where Sreco Acimovic was, but then can you confirm that you did not hear any discussion between Sreco Acimovic and whoever was with him in that office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Never. I didn't hear that ever. The conversation or -- although he had a Motorola and a phone, but I wasn't interested in that. You understand. And Sreco's highness did not allow soldiers to come to -- close to him. That was off limits.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you don't know who, if anyone, was in that office with Acimovic at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And while you were waiting in the hallway, you never saw anybody coming and going from that office, did you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No, nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I take it that you yourself did not participate in any conversation between Sreco Acimovic and whoever was with him at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And are you aware that Sreco Acimovic testified before this Trial Chamber earlier this year?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And where did you learn that Sreco Acimovic testified?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I heard it over the TV. I heard his words. I heard his words, although I came too late, since I work 10 to 12, sometimes even 15 hours a day. If you want to have a living, you have to work that much back in our parts. Some might even earn a better living working only half an hour than me working 15 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, I think it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perfect. Thank you. We'll have a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Welcome back, sir. I have a few more questions, and we will try to finish today so that you can go home as early as possible.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: When Sreco Acimovic testified, he said that he did not remember that you drove him to Rocevic. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Who else could have driven him when there was no other vehicle in the battalion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I just had an objection to the form of the question but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move then.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And sir, when Sreco Acimovic testified, he said that you were standing close to him when pressure was exercised on him. Do you recall any such pressure being exercised on Sreco Acimovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No. Not in my presence. But I wasn't present in the office or when that man in the jeep arrived. I was -- I was not present when they were together.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when Sreco Acimovic testified, he said that he really could not remember how you found yourself in the school. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: That is impossible. In this room, I concede that over 90 per cent must have children. I can swear on the lives of my children -- may I not find them alive when I return home if it wasn't me who drove Sreco there. I drove him because the battalion had no other vehicle. There was an old Lada Niva, and Sreco didn't go anywhere in that vehicle. It was only me who drove him in my car and using my own fuel and fuel was five marks a litre at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, when Sreco Acimovic testified, he said that you overheard his conversation with another officer and that you said, "Well, we have trucks that can be used to drive the prisoners away." Did you ever offer trucks to drive the prisoners away to Sreco Acimovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: That's ridiculous. It is clear who was in charge of requisitioned vehicles and who can order a driver to drive a requisitioned vehicle somewhere. I, as a private, the driver of a commander, was not in a position to order anyone anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Also during his testimony and this one I will quote for the benefit of my colleague from page 12969 to 12970, talking about Djoko Nikolic, Sreco Acimovic said the following: "This soldier, Dragan Jovic, who was nearby and who listened in our conversation, he said, and I noted earlier, that he thought that one of those soldiers, Djoko Nikolic, was at home because this man was in private business." Did you ever suggest to Sreco Acimovic that Djoko Nikolic could be used to transport the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I said that once. For five days, I was in Malesic during the campaign in Srebrenica and the breakthrough from Srebrenica via Baljkovica to Muslim territory around Tuzla. I didn't even know where my wife and children were, let alone some -- who would be in what --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, in your statement, or your interview, you said that when you were waiting in the hallway, that Sreco Acimovic spent a long time in that office. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you also mentioned in your interview that according to you, when you looked into the gym, you estimated that there was from 100 to 150 prisoners. Is that correct? Is that your estimate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I may have overestimated the number but it was -- it's a rough number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when you went home, in your interview you stated that one of the reasons was that you took a pill because you had a headache. Do you recall saying this in your interview?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I don't know who did not have a headache on that day. Everybody must have had it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I'd like to know the -- after coming back from your house, to the best of your recollection, what time would it have been?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, between 12.00 and 1.00 p.m. or 1.30. I don't know exactly. Thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And also in your -- when you testified earlier about this man that had a conversation with Sreco Acimovic when you came back, you stated that he was there for a very short time. Is that -- do you recall saying this in your interview?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I remember. I was absent some 40 minutes to 60 minutes because I went home to take a bath, change, and take a pill because of my headache. When that vehicle arrived, I wasn't there. Whether they were in the school or not, I don't know. I only know that they were standing in front of the goal of the soccer pitch, and I passed them by at a distance of some 10 or 15 metres, walking toward my car.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'd like to have Exhibit 3D100 on e-court, please. Sir, I'm going to show you a sketch. I'd like you to -- which will appear in front of you. I'd like you to tell me if you recognise this sketch. Can we reduce it a bit so we have the complete sketch? Like this. It's perfect. Sir, do you recognise this sketch?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Turn it the other way. Not that way. Now it's good. Now it's good. I know this sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: This is a sketch of the school at Rocevic, at the sports grounds, two residential buildings, across the road from the school a shop, and the road toward my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask to you make some markings on this sketch with the assistance of the usher. I explained to you when we met that there was a special pen that will be give town. I'd like you to write the number 1 with a circle around it where you parked your car that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Can you put -- make a circle around that number?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks] It's a little big but all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And can you mark a number 2 where the United Nations carrier was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Number 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And can you put a number 3 where that conversation took place between the unknown man and Sreco Acimovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Number 3. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And if you can put a number 4 where the Campagnola, that four wheel drive jeep, where that was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks] On the road. The village road.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And can you put a number 5 where the door by which you entered the school, when you came in the first time, when you arrive for the first time in Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And can you put an arrow and the number 6 indicating the way towards your house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. In the bottom right corner, can you put your initials, DJ, and put today's date, which is 21 November 2007?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks] Which date is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: 21 November.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: The 21st of November?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I confused that too. [Marks] 21.11.07.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yes. Just one question, we can save this, please. Just one question. Where you indicated the one with your car, would I be right in saying that your car was further between those two buildings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, inside, or rather, in there, because there is enough space.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the moment at which Sreco Acimovic came to tell you that the prisoners had to be killed, is that shortly after this unknown man left? Was that when this took place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Right after that, and I believe that Sreco Acimovic never did anything on his own. He only obeyed orders. And he didn't listen to his subordinates, to his soldiers. He respected Mr. Pandurevic more than his own father.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would I be right in saying that -- you mentioned already that you told Sreco Acimovic that it was wrong, what he was -- what he wanted to do. Can you just explain how you felt when you were told about this order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: That is impossible to say in one sentence. It is a huge stress when you're told something like that, because I expected an exchange, because we are not talking about one man or two men. It's a greater number of people. And I tried to tell him somehow, and he was probably lost, but he must certainly have had an order. But he said, "It's an order. We have to do it." And I don't know from whom that order was because I never had a Motorola or access to a telephone or a telegraph. I couldn't send or receive any such messages, nor could I sleep there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And in your -- during your interview, you stated the following about Sreco Acimovic, that he was a man who would always render his orders, orders that he would always receive, 120 per cent, not even 100 per cent. Does that correspond to your knowledge of Sreco Acimovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. And that can also be corroborated by Mr. Pandurevic. Whenever the -- our forces went, were deployed, and we know where they were deployed from Zvornik over Sarajevo over to Krajina, Sreco Acimovic always sent as many soldiers as he was required to, possibly he would even send more but never fewer. He was a car electrician but in the army he was a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And again during your interview on page 12, you stated the following about Acimovic: "He's a tough man. He is not cooperative. He is only -- he is only important for himself. He thinks that he is the smartest and one cannot talk to him. You cannot, in discussion with him, contribute in any way. He has his opinion and nobody else matters." Does that correspond to your knowledge of Sreco Acimovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly. He could only talk with a high-ranking officers, but he wouldn't talk to soldiers. There was no discussion with soldiers. They were -- they had to execute his orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when I look at -- when you say you returned home and you saw Veljko Ivanovic, you don't know who asked or who ordered him to come to the school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No. Veljko had his commander, in the rear, who decided where a vehicle should go and who should sign the relevant order. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, during that first trip to Kozluk, it was Ivanovic who was driving the truck; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the only reason you went with him was because you were familiar with that area because you were a private entrepreneur before the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Sreco ordered me to go with Veljko Ivanovic to show him the way on his first trip there, and Sreco, before the war, also transported gravel in a tractor just like myself. He also knew the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. And on that first trip, in the back of this truck, my understanding, based on your testimony, is that there was some prisoners on the truck as well as three or four military police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And during your interview, you stated, on page 5, concerning these soldiers, and I will read what you said, "So I did not know these soldiers. They were military police. They said that they were from the Bratunac Brigade, but I never saw them and I would not be able to recognise them today." Is that a fair summary of your --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: -- testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, those -- to the best of your knowledge, those three or four military police who were on that first trip, they were part of the military police that were guarding the prisoners at the school, it was the same people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when you returned to the school, you had to make two trips to get the truck from Mico Stanojevic because his wife and mother had refused to give you the keys; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, are you sure that Sreco Acimovic did go with to you get that vehicle the second time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: 200 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, about Djoko Nikolic, you mentioned in your testimony today that you still do not remember whether he was there or not; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. That man never helped me or harmed me, but I don't remember. Nor did we talk about that any -- at any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So if Sreco Acimovic testified that you proposed the name of Djoko Nikolic, this does not correspond to what you remember; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: That's a lie. That's a lie. How should I have known where Djoko Nikolic was, whether he was at home? I had my car to care about, and Sreco was in a position to command both me and my car. And he also gave orders to go to the front line and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Only a few more questions. During the time that you were at Rocevic school, and the trips you made to Kozluk, I take it that did you not see any other member of the 2nd Battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: When I came to Rocevic with Sreco, I saw nobody. Later, I couldn't see anyone because I drove a truck. And later on, certainly not, in front of the school, only the military police and a few -- you're talking about the executions, I went there with Veljko on the first trip, and when I went there with the vehicle of Mico Stanojevic, there were also soldiers there, but about the rest, no, just military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And these soldiers, you did not recognise any of them, and they were unknown to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I know five military police at the most who were from the surroundings but not more. I know who was killed and who was injured at Baljkovica. But the military police, or 99 per cent of them, were at Baljkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you just mentioned that you, to use your words --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: The Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yes. So you just testified that you know five military police at the most who were from the surroundings, from Zvornik Brigade, but these people, you did not see them at Rocevic or at Kozluk; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. I didn't know that as military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I take it that you know who Drago Nikolic is, maybe not personally, but you know what he looks like; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I take it that you never saw Drago Nikolic in and/or around Rocevic school or Kozluk on those days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the name Drago Nikolic was never mentioned either by Sreco Acimovic or by anyone else during this period or during that day in 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I know that I didn't see him, and I cannot guarantee for Sreco Acimovic, especially bearing in mind his statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I'm not talking whether someone else saw him, but the name was not mentioned when in your presence on that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No, nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to mention a few names to see if you can confirm that these people who are members of the 2nd Battalion command, Zdravko Ilic, he's a member of the 2nd Battalion command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And Stevo Savic is also a member of the 2nd Battalion command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He's the deputy battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And Mile Lazarevic is also somebody who is from the 2nd Battalion command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know his exact duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And --?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Desk officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And Zico?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Zico Pisic, his father's name is Stevo. He was commander of the rear. Because there were two men of that name. That's why I'm saying that this one is the son of Stevo, and he was the commander of the rear. And I remember Vujo, who was in charge of moral guidance.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued]... Vujo Lazarevic correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Vujo Lazarevic, yes, yes. And Zoran Jovic, another desk officer or administrator for the payroll in the military. That's what I can remember at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, bearing in mind these people at the command, my question is the following: Either on those days in July of 1995 or at any other time since then, you never heard or learned about a telegram being sent to the 2nd Battalion command asking Sreco Acimovic to send volunteers from the 2nd Battalion to execute the prisoners; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No. I never heard of that. I heard that on the TV when he was in the court proceedings, that he was asked to set aside an execution platoon. He said that there were no available soldiers and that's correct. Therefore, that's definitely not true. I never heard of that. I never heard of that telegram or saw anything. A lot of the soldiers from the 2nd Battalion were seconded because things weren't looking up. The soldiers knew that. The officers knew that. Because things did not go as planned.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you yourself, sir, personally, when you took those people to Kozluk, you never saw or heard any executions taking place when you were there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: When taking -- either when you were driving with Ivanovic or when you were driving your truck from --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: When you went to Kozluk, you never saw executions yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No. That's correct. I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And just maybe one last question, the -- in your interview you stated that it is Acimovic who selected Kozluk as the execution site; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: He said that the executions should take place at Kozluk. Whether this was ordered to him or whether this was his decision, the location, the site, I can't talk about that. I wouldn't want to err.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: If I can just have one quick minute to check my notes, I think I'm done, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, no questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krgovic? None? Or Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: None, as indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just two or three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. Leave about two minutes before the time because Mr. McCloskey wishes to address the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, I want to begin by asking you a question or two about --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: -- the day before you drove to Kozluk. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The gentleman who is putting questions to you is Defence counsel for Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You've told us that on that day, that that was the first time that you heard about the presence of prisoners at Rocevic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And at the time that you heard, you were at or near the command of the 2nd Battalion at Malesici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: In front of the command at the place where the soldiers, the logistics people, gathered. Not the check-point but the gate at the entrance into the headquarters, some 10, 20 metres away. So I was in front of the command. In a garden, let's put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And as far as you were aware, the person who brought that message conveyed it to the people inside the command building; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know who conveyed it to the command. The man who came up from Rocevici, he told those who were gathered there. We were listening to the fighting that was going on day and night. We were sitting there and we couldn't hear a single good -- a single good piece of news. We were listening to the fighting. Now, who conveyed this to Sreco, if anyone from the people who were at the gate conveyed that to him, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But in any event, the following day, you went with him to Rocevic; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And it appeared to you, didn't it, during the course of that journey, that he was surprised to learn that prisoners were being held in the school at Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't put it that way. I think that it was maybe through a telegram or some other sort of communications device, he had known already of these prisoners. That's my opinion. He would be the one who would know best if he received it in writing or in some other way, because he had all of that, writing, the oral information, Motorolas. He had everything with him at the command. Which was operational.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But when you arrived at the school, the first thing that he did was to get Boro Lakic to open the office for him so he had access to telephones; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you see the office opened by Boro Lakic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I know that there was the man there who was in charge of the school. He had the keys to the teachers' offices because after all, the school books, with the students' marks were there, stationery, and he was in charge of that to make sure nothing went missing, and I'm sure that Boro opened the door to the office since there was a telephone set in the office. Sreco had his Motorola. Now, what the range of a Motorola is, others know that. I don't. Of course, one can do whatever one needs to with a telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I think it's right, isn't it, that you remained at the school for about an hour before you went home to take a pill?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And during that time, there was no question of Sreco Acimovic giving orders for prisoners to be killed or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But when you returned, there was a jeep vehicle there and a man you hadn't seen before conversing with Sreco Acimovic on the playground; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And it was after that conversation that you saw that there was the first discussion about prisoners being killed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: From Sreco, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And following that, you were dispatched to the house of a man called Draskovic, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you've told us you were an officer without rank. Did you have any authority to give him an order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No, not to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But Sreco Acimovic would have given -- had the authority to give him an order, would he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't believe he would have one in relation to him because Draskovic was not a member of the army. After his brother had been killed, he was released from military duty because I believe that the rule was that where one of the brothers was killed, the other one should be placed -- assigned to the rear or released from duty, especially if they are poor. And I know that Draskovic's brother and the other two men who were with them who were killed, their bodies had never been found. They had never been given a burial. Today, the Muslims live there and nobody made the effort of finding their bodies and having their bones laid to rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How many more --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: This is the last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But when he declined the invitation to take part in executing prisoners, nothing was done about it; is that right? Sreco didn't go along and say, "You've got to do this"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: To whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: To Mr. Draskovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JOVIC
utterances.text: No. He didn't ask for Draskovic. He sent me to ask Draskovic whether he would want to go and execute Muslims. And my conclusion was that he got this idea because he believed that perhaps Draskovic would want to take vengeance for his brother who had been killed and whose body has never been found, and how many years have passed since? He did not order anything. He merely sent me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question was whether, when Draskovic refused to take part in the executions, whether he was punished or whether any action was taken against him. And your answer is no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was on a voluntary basis. Practically to enable him to revenge his brother. That's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Nicholls, do you have a re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't have any further questions for you, Mr. Jovic, which means you can go. Thank you for coming over to give testimony and we wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will do the exhibits tomorrow. In the meantime, who is going to address the Trial Chamber? Mr. Nicholls? Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour it's a matter for scheduling. It can be in open session if we don't use names. I sent out an e-mail to my colleagues that I believe was forwarded to Your Honours staff that we may have a change tomorrow. I have not got any new information on the health status of the witness who was scheduled to be next. I'll check on that after court right now. My indications that I received earlier today is that he was quite ill, so our proposal was to continue the cross-examination of Mr. Blaszczyk which had been scheduled for Friday in any event. In other words, to swap these two witnesses and to give the scheduled Witness 190 time to recuperate and that would be the plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So we'll see what happens tomorrow. Thank you, have a nice evening. See you tomorrow in the afternoon at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 22nd day of November, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.
